newsitem.title: FRANCE: Italy's STET joins Bouygues in French telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Italy's STET joins Bouygues in French telecoms.

text.p: French building company Bouygues said on Thursday that Italy's STET was joining it and Germany's VEBA to set up a rival telecommunications system to France Telecom after liberalisation of the sector in 1998.
Bouygues said it was setting up a 51/49 percent joint-venture with STET.
STET will also enter the share capital of the BDP holding company which holds 51 percent of Bouygues Telecom. STET will pay 1.71 billion francs to buy into BDT.
Italy's STET joins Bouygues in French telecoms
After the capital increase, which will take place is stages in 1996 and 1997, Bouygues will have 59.5 percent of Bouygues Telecom, Jean-Claude Decaux International 20.9 percent and STET 19.6 percent.
VEBA has a 15 percent stake in Bouygues Telecom.
Bouygues said the first action of the new group was to jointly bid for the operation of the telephone network of state-ralroads group SNCF.
Last month, Generale des Eaux said it was forming a special telecoms unit CEGETEL with British Telecommunications Plc, SBC of the U.S. and Mannesman AG of Germany.
Bouygues already operates France third mobile telephone network, in rivalry with Generale's SFR and France Telecom.
